alignments.note: Supplied determiner joins the noun under rule 15.

Supplied relative over a verbless clause with a written antecedent and no relative morpheme; added under rule 55, exactly as at PRO.30.12 and PRO.30.24. Rule 41's articleless attributive does not reach it: גִּבּוֹר predicates of לַיִשׁ rather than modifying it inside one nominal expression, as the parallel `הַנְּמָלִים עַם לֹא־עָז` of PRO.30.25 shows, and the relative's scope runs on over the coordinated finite clause.
Predicate adjective with the construction-supplied copula under rule 20; head on the word carrying the lexeme.
The ASV writes no *the* before *beasts*, so the assimilated article is unrepresented under rule 29.
Verb with its particle *away*, which completes the שׁוב lexeme; discontinuous around the negative under rule 25.
מִפְּנֵי rendered by the single *for*; the preposition and its construct noun share one unit headed on the construct noun under rule 30.

review_notes: מִפְּנֵי is fused under rule 30 because the ASV writes one preposition for the pair; splitting it would leave one of the two morphemes unrepresented.

Reconciliation patch: *which* is now added under rule 55 and *is mightiest* belongs to the adjective with the copula of rule 20, matching PRO.30.12 and PRO.30.24. Rule 41's articleless attributive was the competing reading and is set aside because the Hebrew writes a predication — the same shape is rendered as a main clause at 30.25 and 30.26, and the English relative governs the coordinated finite clause as well.
